additional_info.subject: RE: ID0373506-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / P7 312547889/07] Charging issue CRM:00643000857
additional_info.body:
Hi Florent,
Greetings of the day!
We have analyzed the logs and found that the charging session was aborted when the EV SOC was around 80-82%, with no issues detected on the charger side. While we acknowledge that the EV has a maximum power capacity of 115kW, the logs I’ve shared below demonstrate that the EV functions as the Master & charger functions as Slave. The charger provided the current and voltage that the EV demanded.
As you can see from the multiple session logs, the EV’s target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to 80% SOC using CC, and then it switches to CV mode. During this phase, the EV's target current drops to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing.
Based on this analysis, we conclude that there is no issue with the EVSE. I hope this addresses your concerns. If there are no further questions, shall we proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
